observation.visible_scene: An outdoor grassy clearing bordered by trees, with a small white container sitting in the background. In the foreground, on a patch of dark charred ground scattered with pale ash, an open brown cardboard shipping box (printed logo visible) rests stationary. The left/rear portion of the box is on fire: a column of yellow-orange flames rises from a mass of blackened, curled material inside that section. The right/main body of the box is not burning, and a piece of white paper protrudes from an opening on its right side.
visible_changes: The fire is already burning at the first frame and continues throughout; no ignition onset or extinguishing is shown.

The flame column continuously flickers, changing height, width, and shape from frame to frame (taller and narrower at some moments, e.g. around t=0.0 and t=0.83-1.10; broader and lower-leaning at others, e.g. around t=0.35-0.55).
The flames rise roughly vertically from the burning left section, sometimes tilting slightly leftward, consistent with turbulent combustion rather than the box moving.

The cardboard box, the white paper on its right, the blackened mass inside, and the ash pile remain in fixed positions relative to the frame; no collapse, translation, or deformation of the box structure is visible within the excerpt.
The background (white container, trees, grass) stays in the same image positions across frames, indicating the camera is essentially stationary.
outside_clip_unknowns: How and when the fire was started, and what material is inside the burning section.
Whether the unburnt right side of the box will later ignite or the structure will collapse after this segment.
The full duration of the burn beyond t=2.76 s.
uncertain_details: The identity of the black curled material (charred plastic vs. burnt cardboard) cannot be confirmed.
The slight leftward lean of the flame at times may reflect air movement, but the cause is not determinable from the frames.
Any very small camera drift cannot be fully ruled out, though background cues suggest the view is static.
